strata-bands.look: Agate default on one setting: thick bands of differing gray with dark thin seams and fine striations inside them. On a single Perlin it reads as polished agate at once, on Worley F1 as malachite with cusps between the ring systems, on a tilted gradient as sediment, and on FBm and warped fields as ragged banded stone. On ridged it gets blobby and is the weakest of the fields tried. My first tuned default (lam 0.25) looked like fingerprint rings; turning laminae far down and widening bands is what made it read as stone. The striations are regular sines, a little mechanical when zoomed. Timber profile: mostly light with thin dark latewood lines that build up on one side. On stretched Perlin and on GrowthAge it reads as sawn wood. Stretched axis-aligned Perlin also shows horizontal row seams from the Perlin lattice (visible about 40 percent down sheet_timber), which is a fault of that source, not of the remap; rings and GrowthAge do not show it. PLAIN TRUTH: for agate the stock graph AddDimension(field) + DomainAxisScale(0,0) + FBm(Value) is a real rival: soft and pretty, without seams or sharp edges; the node is richer but not a different league (strata_bands_vs_real_graph). For wood the profile is a clear win: a real stock graph with equal sawtooth reads as zebra stripes (its ring density is about twice my panel because the source scale did not match), and the node itself with jitter and per-ring contrast off, at matched density, reads the same way, so hashed ring widths and contrast are what sell it. Per-ring lateral slices are subtle at the default 0.4. It removes height meaning, so it is for masks and textures, not terrain.
strata-bands.dims: 2D measured and rendered. 3D rendered with vol and an XZ slice. 4D not built; it only adds hashes over Source and Lateral, so it follows those sources (reasoned, not run).
strata-bands.range: agate -0.881..0.927 over 8 seeds on warped and -0.914..0.926 on single Perlin. Timber at jit 0.9 -0.664..0.973, skewed light by design.
strata-bands.node_shape: Not a separate node. Same band lattice as StrataTerrace, so one Strata node with Profile enum Caprock | Agate | Timber | Sawtooth | Layer Value, plus Lateral source, Lateral Amount, Seam Density and Contrast for non-height profiles.
strata-bands.port_notes: Measured scalar 418 ns on single Perlin (8.38x perlin2) and 967 ns on the warped default source (19.35x), including source and Lateral, inflated by std::map lookups. The real stock timber rival benched 8.39 / 14.11 / 21.52 ns AVX2 for 2D/3D/4D with the source evaluated twice and no cache; the earlier run measured 7.72 ns for the 1D lookup graph against 0.92 for Perlin. c0ratio 4.69 agate, 5.30 on Perlin, 2.54 timber at 30 bands: reasoned to be steep thin rings because band envelopes meet at boundaries; no step-size test run here. Cap jitter below 1 so a ring cannot collapse (reasoned; the cap only moved timber c0ratio from 2.11 to 2.54). Bands alias on steep sources.

The polished agate look on single Perlin is the best image and neither stock lookup matches it (Value lookup is soft, CellularValue lookup is flat). Cheapest honest packaging: Terrace gains Thickness Jitter and a Profile enum (Step | Caprock | Agate | Timber) plus an optional Lateral source, at about 1 ns over the source; the caprock profile is then also covered. Not a separate node.

Wide view at seed 2024 shows no lattice imprint but fine bands moire. Timber with jit=0,ajit=0,lat=0 still reads as wood, so the hashed ring width is a mild refinement, not the win claimed. The polished agate on single Perlin is the best texture image in the family and neither stock lookup matches it. Everything here is a 1D profile of the source on a jittered band lattice, which is Terrace with a different profile: package as Terrace members (Thickness Jitter, Profile enum Step | Caprock | Agate | Timber, optional Lateral source) at about 1 ns over the source, not as a separate Strata node. Bands alias on steep sources at any count above about 10 per unit.

master.one_liner: Remaps any field through a jittered 1D band lattice with an asymmetric ring profile and an independent source slice per band: tree rings, agate, sediment, onion layers.
master.look:
Look-tested (m=2 and m=3). Agate-like banding over warped fields, and with a GrowthAge source very believable plain-sawn wood: thick and thin rings, each ring with its own mottling. Sediment cliffs over a Gradient. Very different from Terrace and PingPong, both of which are uniform.
[Strata, libs-modifiers] Look-tested (mode 12). Monotone: subtly uneven sedimentary terraces. Agate: dramatic black/white banding following contours, with thin dark seams, like polished agate or oil film; clearly different from Terrace and PingPong on the sheet. On a Gradient + warp source in 3D it should give rock strata (not rendered).
master.algorithm:
s=Source(p)*Bands. i=floor(s). Band boundaries b(k)=k+Jit*(rnd(hash1(k))-.5). Evaluate b(i), b(i+1), and via masks b(i-1) or b(i+2) to find band k with b(k)<=s<b(k+1) (3 hashes, 2 Selects). u=(s-b(k))/(b(k+1)-b(k)). Envelope v=u^e*(1-smoothstep(1-Drop,1,u)): slow earlywood rise, sharp latewood drop. Per band: amp a(k)=.4+.6*rnd; lateral eval L=Lateral(p + Offset(k)) once, at a domain offset hashed from k. Output a*v*(1+Lat*L). Because v is 0 at both band ends, the jump in k and in L is invisible, so one lateral eval suffices with no blend. Output clamped and scaled.

[StrataBands, signal-phase] t=Freq*S(p)+Offset. For o in 0..Octaves-1: x=t*2^o; i=Floor(x); u=smoothstep(x-i); a=hash1(i,seed+o); b=hash1(i+1,seed+o); sum+=g^o*lerp(a,b,u).
Out=normalised sum to [-1,1].
Variants: Sharpness applied to u; band width jitter by warping t with a first-octave value; hard sync: per-band integer ratio n=1+hash(floor(t))%R and an inner Tri of n*fract(t), which gives sub-bands that change per band (needs a window to stay continuous).
master.why_new: Terrace and PingPong apply a uniform periodic function, and rings never differ from each other. There is no way in the graph to hash on the value of a field. The per-band source slice, with a zero-envelope seam trick, gives independently mottled layers for the cost of one extra eval.
master.simd_plan: Cheap: 3 1D hashes, Select, one Pow (or fixed u^2/u^3 polynomial if e is an enum), one Source eval, one Lateral eval: about 1x Perlin over source cost. Dimension agnostic since Source and Lateral do the dimension work: GenT pack with offset added on all axes. 4D automatically works and tiles.
master.continuity: C0 everywhere the source is continuous, because the envelope vanishes at band ends. Kink at the drop. Measured c0ratio 2.46 only because of steep drops at high band counts; slope scales with Bands*|grad Source|/Drop.
master.params: Source (generator), Lateral (generator, optional), Bands (hybrid), Band Jitter, Profile Power, Drop, Lateral Amount, Amp Jitter, Lateral Offset. Hybrid: Lateral Amount, Drop, Bands if the caller accepts ring shifts where it varies.
master.risks:
Source with near-zero gradient gives wide flat bands. Hybrid Bands shifts all rings far from zero, so it causes fast movement. Measured range 1.41 before normalisation, needs a clamp or a constant divide. Pow can be expensive per lane, so prefer the polynomial.
[Strata, libs-modifiers] Monotone differs only mildly from Terrace unless Jitter is high, so the Agate mode carries the visual novelty. Agate removes height meaning, so it is for masks and textures. Output of Monotone can exceed [-1,1] slightly by Jitter/2K. Sharpness 0 limit produces a hard step, as with Terrace.
[ValueStrata, hierarchy-multiscale] Bands alias on steep sources because frequency scales with source gradient. Output std is low (about 0.2-0.3), so it needs a measured scale. Feedback barely changed the look in the proto.
master.cost_note: Cheap: 3 1D hashes, Select, one Pow (or fixed u^2/u^3 polynomial if e is an enum), one Source eval, one Lateral eval: about 1x Perlin over source cost.
master.variant_notes: Hash on the value itself. Options: monotone terraces and agate per-band gray (Strata), per-band lateral source with a zero-envelope seam trick (StrataBands, texture), fractal column with Drift and Feedback (ValueStrata).

queue.name: StrataBands
queue.reason: Jittered 1D band lattice with asymmetric profile and per-band lateral slice: wood and agate from any field at ~1 Perlin overhead. Pairs with growth-age.

growth-age.look: Through the Timber remap the sheet reads straight away as a planed pale board: long fine grain, a cathedral arch series, round knots with closed ring eyes and grain visibly deflecting round them. Best on seeds 99, 1337 and 7 (a big eye knot); seed 42 has only a cathedral and no small knot at this zoom, so what lands in frame varies. Board sweep goes from nearly straight grain with one long thin flame at 0.2 to wide plain-sawn arches at 4. Vol at iso 0.58 shows a timber block with grain grooves that agree across faces and a knot on top; thin splintery sheets appear at higher iso. Raw age alone is a smooth dull gradient, it must go through a remap to be seen at all. The remap matters a lot: the old bright sawtooth was line art, the 1D lookup graph on the same field looks like banded stone more than wood, PingPong and equal sawtooth are zebra stripes (strata_rings_on_growth_age). Knots and cathedral arches come from this field and cannot be had by warping noise; plain stretched Perlin through the Timber remap gives wood without them. Single trunk, so it is non-stationary and far from the axis age saturates.
growth-age.dims: 2D (slice z=board) and 3D measured and rendered. 4D not built; the catalogue plan of adding w to the ring offset was not tested. A true 4D torus tile looks hard for one trunk axis (reasoned, not run), so tiling should go through the plank form or a tile-domain node.
growth-age.range: raw age through clamp(age/6): -0.304..1.0 over 8 seeds; far coordinates saturate to exactly 1.0 (std 0) because a single trunk is non-stationary. Timber remap -0.679..1.066, needs a divide or clamp.
growth-age.node_shape: Knot Spacing, Knot Length, Knot Growth, Knot Speed, Knot Sharpness, Knot Tilt, Knot Probability, Trunk Wobble, Wobble Frequency, Board Offset (hybrid), Max Age; optional Plank Width and Length for the stationary form.
growth-age.port_notes: Measured scalar 233 ns raw (4.56x perlin2) and 456 ns (9.18x) with Timber remap, Lateral and fibre evals, inflated by std::map lookups. c0ratio 8.00 is the raw node; through Timber at 10 rings it is 3.14 with max slope 351 per unit, reasoned to be thin steep rings near the pith (no step-size test run). Window proven in the earlier run by a diff test against a 9 cell search: exactly 0 at kspace=2, klen=3 over 16 units at 4 axis offsets and 3 seeds; kspace=1.6 fails by up to 0.04 at klen=3 and 0.736 at klen=6. Reasoned bound that matched: 1.2*Spacing >= Length*sin(Tilt) + Growth*((1-Speed)*Length + Sharpness), so clamp Spacing from it. Use DomainOffset or the Plank form for variety. The time-field idea comes from published work (from memory Larsson et al. 2022), implemented from the catalogue formula only.

critic.notes: The only idea in the family a graph cannot reach: knots with closed ring eyes and grain deflecting round them, cathedral arches from the board offset. Raw age is a dull clamped gradient, so it only works through a ring remap, which is a Terrace-like profile. A single trunk is non-stationary; the plank form fixes that at the cost of visible rectangular seams. Wood is a material texture, off the main terrain use of the library, and 4D tiling has no obvious form. Worth keeping as an example graph or sample, not a core node.

tournament.notes: Re-measured: scalar 455 ns with the Timber remap (9.2x perlin2), 233 ns raw (4.7x); range -0.684..1.059 over 8 seeds; c0ratio 1.71 with max slope 651 at the default, which is the thinnest jittered ring and not a jump but it aliases at any normal zoom. Reads as wood with knots on every seed tried, and the knots and cathedral arches are the one thing in the family a stock graph cannot reach. Against it: raw age is a dull clamped gradient that only works through a ring remap, a single trunk is non-stationary (the wide view is one horizontal band with knots repeating at the 2 unit spacing), the plank form shows rectangular seams, the iso 0.58 volume is splintery sheets rather than a block, 4D tiling has no obvious form, and wood is a material texture off the main terrain use. Keep as an example or sample graph, not a core node.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 5 ns in 2D/3D/4D for raw age (4 1D value noises, 3 knots each with 1 hash and 1 sqrt).

artist-terrain.note: Reads as planed board with knots and cathedral arches on every seed; thinnest ring aliases (max slope 651). Plank floor variant is the useful form.

artist-material.note: Real wood with knots and cathedral arches, which nothing else reaches. Thin rings alias at the default and raw age needs the remap.

voxel-engineer.note: Reads as wood with knots, but non-stationary and c0 1.71. Plank form is the usable one.

maintainer.note: Through the Timber remap it reads as a planed board with cathedral arches and knots, ~5 ns est raw. Wood is a top-requested material; the thin ring (max slope 651) and no 4D hold it back. I would still look at it before most showcases.

graphics-researcher.note: Wood with knots, cathedral arches and grain deflecting round knots on every seed; the plank form makes it stationary. Known target, decent execution.

creative.note: Actual wood with knots and cathedral arches. The block volume is astonishing. Thin rings will alias.

master.one_liner: A 3D growth-time field for wood: trunk radius smooth-min'ed with knot cones hashed along the axis, so rings wrap around knots and slicing gives cathedral grain.
master.look: Look-tested through StrataBands (m=3, rings=30). Excellent cathedral arches and grain flowing around knots, with closed ring islands where a branch crosses the board. The most recognisable real wood I have seen from a pointwise formula. Output alone is a smooth field, also usable as a growth mask for horn, bone or shell with different kernels.
master.algorithm: Grain along x. Trunk wobble: y'=y+W*n1(x), z'=z+W*n2(x) from low-frequency 1D noise. r=sqrt(y'^2+z'^2). age=r. For the 3 nearest knot cells along x (cell=floor(x/Spacing)): knot origin at (kx(h),0,0), azimuth from h, axis a tilted Tilt toward +x. q=p-origin, t=clamp(dot(q,a),0,KnotLength), db=|q-t*a|, kage=db/Grow+0.9*t+rnd*Offset. Polynomial smin: k=sat(.5+.5*(age-kage)/Sharp), age=lerp(age,kage,k)-Sharp*k*(1-k). Output: ScaleOutput(age,0,MaxAge). 2D slice: z=Board (hybrid), so Board Offset chooses plain-sawn versus quarter-sawn. 4D: w added to the ring offset so it stays a real 4D function. Feed into StrataBands.
master.why_new: Plain wood recipes (rings of distance plus noise) produce no knots, and noise warps cannot make grain deflect around a specific feature. This field is the hard part of wood. Researchers have published a very similar time-field approach (from memory: Larsson et al., procedural wood with knots, 2022), but I do not know of a noise library node for it.
master.simd_plan: 2D: 2 trunk 1D noises, 3 knots each with 1 sqrt and 5-6 ops, about 1.5-2x Perlin 2D. Same in 3D as the formula is 3D already, so 3D is the natural form and costs only slightly more than Perlin 3D. Knot window: 3 cells along x with one hash each, no 2D lattice at all.
master.continuity: C1 inside, except at the axis where r has a cone tip (C0) and where the capped t bends. Measured c0ratio 3.91 through a steep StrataBands, not through this node itself.
master.params: Knot Spacing, Knot Growth, Sharpness, Tilt, Knot Length, Trunk Wobble, Board Offset (hybrid), Max Age. Hybrid: Board Offset, Trunk Wobble.
master.risks: Non-stationary by nature, a single trunk around the axis, so it is meant to be used inside TileSplit Interior or with DomainOffset. Knot influence widens with radius, so uncapped cones leave the 3 cell window and seam; KnotLength must cap it (proto had no cap and looked clean at board offsets below 0.6, but this is not proven at large radius). Age is unbounded without the cap on distance from axis.
master.cost_note: 2D: 2 trunk 1D noises, 3 knots each with 1 sqrt and 5-6 ops, about 1.5-2x Perlin 2D.

queue.name: GrowthAge
queue.reason: Knot-aware wood growth field, the hard part of wood and not graphable. Single non-stationary trunk, so test instancing through tile-domain or stamp-scatter.

strata-terrace.look: Relief default is now flat-capped mesas and buttes with sheer sides, smooth talus slopes between cliff bands and basins walled by a cliff. Held on the 4 seeds I rendered at the final default (1337, 7, 42, 99), where seed-rolled hardness had given seeds 1337 and 7 mostly plain hills. dipx=0.8: parallel hogback ridges with long dip slopes and scarps on one side. Fold source: curved cliff bands sweeping round the terrain, the most striking 2D view. 3D density with alternating hardness: hoodoos with overhanging caps, but with small detached floating fragments at ledge 0.4 to 0.5. What changed it: the old profile gave every layer a bench and read as modest paddy terraces; the new one gives hard layers a short cliff and then a flat cap, and soft layers keep the source slope and steepen into a talus apron under a hard layer. PLAIN TRUTH about rivals: real fnlab Terrace at matching cliff spacing is an even staircase with no slopes; a real two-Terrace Fade graph softens into bumpy contours and gets no flat caps, though the same two-Terrace formula at a thicker layer (scalar) looks closer: uneven table steps, but no plain slopes between them. Terrace with a very large step and few levels does make mesas on a plain on the one seed I tried, almost like my threshold-hardness test, so isolated mesas alone are not the gain. Tilted Terrace via a graph reaches parallel cuestas with equal rhythm, so tilting alone is not the gain either; the idea's claim that a graph cannot tilt is false. In 3D a REAL stock node graph, density plus two-Terrace sawtooth at ledge 0.22, gives crisp stacked strata with uneven rhythm, far better than the 1D Value baseline used in the earlier run, so the 3D gain is only overhanging caps and per-layer hardness, not sharpness or rhythm. The real gain is the mix of flat caps, cliffs and plain slopes in one stack, with one robust default. Rock detail is not added, it comes from the source.
strata-terrace.dims: 2D measured and rendered. 3D rendered with vol in two forms: the same formula on a 3D source (blobby, not useful) and the density form (good). 4D not built; no lattice, so a GenT pack should work (reasoned, not run). On the tileable torus, linear dip stays periodic but stops being a plane (reasoned, not rendered).
strata-terrace.range: default -1.147..1.281 over 8 seeds with source gain sg=1.7: output tracks the source within a layer, so a port needs a clamp or a measured divide
strata-terrace.node_shape: One Strata node: Source; Layer Thickness; Thickness Jitter; Cliff Fraction; Talus Power; Keep Source; Dip per axis (hybrid); Fold (hybrid); Hard Layer Pattern enum Alternate | Random Per Group; Profile enum Caprock | Agate | Timber | Sawtooth | Layer Value; Lateral source and Lateral Amount for non-height profiles; density offset output for 3D.
strata-terrace.port_notes: Measured scalar 398 ns with the 5 octave default (7.75x perlin2) and 258 ns with 1 octave (5.02x), inflated by std::map lookups. Alternation needs only (k & 1), the cheapest hardness scheme tried and the only one that held on every seed tried. The catalogue's gradient-based talus (1 + dim evals) was dropped in the earlier run because it looked no better and flickered on 5 octaves. Soft-layer Pow can be a polynomial. Sheet stat axis=26.5 although the FFT panel shows no bright cross; I did not explain that number. The density form needs the strata coordinate to exclude the source.

critic.notes: The caprock profile with alternating hard and soft layers is exactly Max( s, Terrace( s, 2T ) ): soft layers keep the source slope where the source is above the staircase, hard layers are the flat tread where the staircase wins, and the Terrace riser is the cliff. The prototyper tested Terrace alone and two-Terrace Fades, never Max. Per-layer hashed thickness and the talus apron are what the node would add and the ablation shows they do not change the picture. If anything ships, it is a Profile enum and a Thickness Jitter on Terrace, not a node.

tournament.notes: Re-measured: c0ratio 8.01, max slope 20.9, range -1.147..1.281 over 8 seeds, far coords fine, scalar 387 ns (7.8x perlin2 with the 5 octave source inside). The default is robust: seeds 555 and 2024 (window 16) show the same mesa, cliff and slope mix, no cherry pick. But the alternating caprock profile is algebraically Max( s, Terrace( s, 2T ) ), the stock graph gives the same picture at 13 ns AVX2 2D, and the parts the node adds (hashed thickness, talus apron) do not show at the default. The hoodoo density form is the one thing a graph does less well (stock density + PingPong gives ledges and overhangs but not clean mushroom caps), and it leaves floating fragments. If anything ships it is a Caprock profile and Thickness Jitter on Terrace.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: source + about 1 ns per lane. With a single Perlin source about 2 / 3.2 / 5.3 ns for 2D/3D/4D.

artist-terrain.note: Mesas and buttes hold on 6 seeds, but Max(S, Terrace(S)) with four stock nodes gives the same picture at 13 ns AVX2. Ship the preset.

artist-material.note: The hoodoo vol is a front-page image. It is Max(s, Terrace(s)) in a stock graph, so a preset.

voxel-engineer.note: Hoodoo vol is the prize; 2D mesas are Max(S, Terrace(S)) from stock at 13.2 ns. Recipe plus 3D density example.

maintainer.note: Mesas look right on 5 seeds but the ablation is indistinguishable from the default and the profile is Max(S, Terrace(S)) plus a Gradient from stock. Preset.

graphics-researcher.note: Algebraically Max(s, Terrace(s)); the stock graph reproduces the default at 13 ns. Folded cliff bands and hoodoos are presets of it.

creative.note: The hoodoo volume is superb. The 2D is merely flat mesas.

master.one_liner: Terrace the source in a tilted, foldable strata coordinate with per-layer hashed thickness and hardness, and a cliff/talus riser whose talus width is measured horizontally: mesas, buttes, cuestas, hogbacks and cliff bands from any height field.
master.look:
Contour-following benches and cliff bands whose spacing follows a tilted plane instead of the horizontal: on a plateau noise it gives mesas and buttes with caprock ledges and talus aprons, with large dip the benches become asymmetric ridges (cuestas/hogbacks), with a Fold source the bands wave like folded sediments. Layers differ in thickness and in bench/cliff proportion, which is what makes it read as rock rather than paddy terraces. Prototyped: Strata/StrataFold.
[StrataFaults, nature-phenomena] Section output reads as a real rock outcrop: bands with varying thickness and tone, with vertical offset blocks at faults. Terrace output gives ledged cliffs with irregular, not equally spaced, benches when applied to a terrain height.
master.algorithm:
Inputs: height source E(p), dip vector (Dip X, Dip Y, hybrid), optional Fold source F(p). Strata coordinate s = E(p) - dot(dip, p) - F(p). Layer boundaries: u = s/T; k = floor(u); jittered boundaries lo_k = k + 0.5*J*rnd11(hash(k)), hi_k = lo_{k+1}; fix k by one compare each way so lo <= u < hi. f = (u-lo)/(hi-lo). Per-layer hardness hard_k = rnd01(hash(k, salt)): riser fraction c = clamp(Cliff*(0.5+hard), 0.05, 0.95) (hard layers = wide bench, short cliff). Horizontal talus: estimate |grad E| by forward differences (dim extra source evals, eps param); talusV = min(Talus*|grad E|/((hi-lo)*T), 0.9) converts a horizontal talus width into a fraction of the layer's value span; tf = clamp(talusV/c, 0, 0.85). rise(f) = 0 for f < 1-c, else r=(f-(1-c))/c, rise = r<tf ? 0.35*r/tf : 0.35 + 0.65*(r-tf)/(1-tf). Output = (lo + rise*(hi-lo))*T + dot(dip,p) + F(p). Variant 'LithologyRetreat' (prototyped, mode 2 of terr_lens2): instead of analytic layers, sample a 3D hardness source K(x, y, E(p)) and displace the sample position downhill by Retreat*softness*gradE/(|gradE|+c) in K steps before re-evaluating E; general but prone to fold-over, so keep the analytic version as the node and mention the other as a DomainWarp variant.

[TiltedStrata, terrain-landforms] c=h(p)+Dip*dot(p,n)+FoldAmp*Fold(p)+Throw(p); t=c/Th; layer boundaries b_i=i+0.4*(rnd(i)-0.5) from a 1D hash; compare t to b_floor(t) to Select the layer i; w=(t-b_i)/(b_(i+1)-b_i). Hardness H_i=hash(i). T(w)=H_i*smoothstep(1-cw,1,w)+(1-H_i)*w, monotone with T(0)=0 and T(1)=1. out=h+Th*(b_(i+1)-b_i)*(T(w)-w)*Strength. Because the bench offset is a function of c, not h, benches climb and descend across terrain with dip. Hard layers form cliffs and benches, soft layers form slopes. 3D density mode: density=(h-y)+OffsetTable(c) where c includes y, giving real overhanging ledges. Output modes: Height, Layer Value for rock colouring.
master.why_new: Terrace steps in value space only: horizontal strata, equal layers, risers that are vertical wherever the source is steep and benches that vanish on slopes. A graph cannot tilt the stepping plane or make the talus width independent of slope because it has no access to the source gradient.
master.simd_plan: 1 + dim source evaluations (forward differences), two integer hashes for the layer boundaries and one for hardness, a handful of Selects for the k fix-up and the piecewise riser. No window. Dimension-agnostic GenT over the pack: dip is per-dimension; 4D works (tileable). Cost ~ (1+dim) x source + ~30 ops: with a Perlin source ~3-5x Perlin in 2D.
master.continuity: C0 whenever rise(0)=0 and rise(1)=1 (adjacent layers meet at hi*T); the cliff is intentionally steep with a user-bounded minimum horizontal width. The probe reports c0ratio 3.6 only because the cliff is narrower than its step h; the construction has no jumps. C1 breaks at bench/riser corners by design.
master.params: Source, Layer Thickness, Thickness Jitter, Hardness Jitter, Cliff Fraction, Talus Width (horizontal units), Dip X/Dip Y (hybrid, so a node can rotate strata regionally), Fold Source (optional GeneratorSource, 0 = none), Gradient Epsilon.
master.risks:
The talus conversion uses a first-order gradient estimate and clamps at 90% of the riser; near saddles of E the estimate is poor but only affects talus width. Per-layer hashing means the layer sequence is global (same stratigraphy everywhere), which is geologically correct but a 2D 'layer id offset' source could vary it. The LithologyRetreat variant overshoots and tears unless Retreat is well under a feature length (measured c0ratio 1.27 at retreat 0.25 with a 4-octave source).
[TiltedStrata, terrain-landforms] Not tested. Partly graph-reachable in simple form, so its value rests on the table and the layer output. Linear Dip grows without bound with distance and float precision on c falls at far coordinates, so wrap c using a large period.
[StrataFaults, nature-phenomena] Discontinuous Section output can alias. Fault cells look like stretched Voronoi, not like true planar faults over large ranges. The value needs per-bed hash on a floor index, which loses float precision at far coordinates.
master.cost_note: Cost ~ (1+dim) x source + ~30 ops: with a Perlin source ~3-5x Perlin in 2D.
master.variant_notes: Terrace in a tilted, folded, faulted coordinate with per-layer hardness. 3D density form gives real overhanging ledges (TiltedStrata). Linear dip is not periodic on the 4D torus.

queue.reason: Tilted foldable strata with hashed hardness and world-unit talus: mesas and cuestas Terrace cannot do (J2 top pick). Looks modest until tuned, so find good defaults.

glacial-troughs.look: Relief: long straight or gently bending U valleys with flat smooth floors and steep walls cut through craggy mountains, with the U section plain at the front edge of the render. It reads as glaciated country on seeds 42 and 7; fjord floor gives steep massifs between flooded troughs and is the most striking view. First versions looked like canals because walls were replaced by a smooth curve. Letting the wall scale the source between floor and surface, and widening the trough with height above the floor, fixed that. Stretching the valley source to 2.5 removed most moats. FLAWS I can see: the wide view still has some closed loop valleys (a moat in the right part of the wide panel on seed 42). Tributaries do not read as a branching system: from above they are short hooks and small hairline scars in the walls (the climb term, which attaches them to parents, leaves cusp tips). Climb 0.8 erased them and left crack lines. Hanging valleys, the catalogue's main promise, are barely visible. Width 0.25 shows the tributary system better from above but weakens the big U section in relief. Branch on against off (relief_nobranch) changes only small tributaries. RIVALS: the plain graph Abs(noise) with no gradient balloons into wide blue plains and clearly loses, so gradient normalisation is a real gain. But a REAL stock node graph, F2-F1 CellularDistance + DomainWarpGradient + PowFloat + Min + Multiply carve, gives straight narrow fjord blocks with true junctions and looks about as strong in a different way (saved as a discovery). The look is good; a dedicated node is not clearly earned beyond gradient normalised width, which iso-distance already provides.
glacial-troughs.dims: 2D measured and rendered. 3D as heightfield density h(x,z)-y renders fine (the black gap at the front of the volume is a trough dropping out of the cube). The pack form on a 3D source, rendered once before the final defaults, cuts thin curved slabs through a cube and is not useful as caves. 4D not built; a GenT pack should work (reasoned, not run).
glacial-troughs.range: default -0.851..1.110 over 8 seeds at seed base 42, -0.944..1.095 at seed base 1337; the source is the upper limit and the floor plus climb the lower one, so a clamp or Output Min/Max is enough
glacial-troughs.node_shape: If shipped at all, an Output = Trough of IsoDistance plus a saved graph that chains tiers: Source; Valley Source; Width (hybrid); Floor (hybrid); Sharpness; Ice Width Gain. Only the side-dependent tributary seed needs a dedicated node, and I saw too little gain from it to justify one.
glacial-troughs.port_notes: Measured scalar 1192 ns (23.8x perlin2, 10.8x worley2) with the 6 octave source and 1035 ns (20.3x) with a 1 octave source and no floor slope, inflated by about 20 std::map lookups. c0ratio 2.17 to 2.81 is not a jump: t_gl_diag takes the 5 largest neighbour differences on 3 seeds at h=1e-3 and they shrink in proportion to h down to 1.5e-5 (worst point 0.04565, 0.01148, 0.00284, 0.00077). It is a short steep wall of slope about 46 per unit against 3.6 for the source alone; 1 tier gives c0ratio 7.71. Tributary seed jumps are hidden by fading a tier to 0 within jfade of the parent axis. The proto's Voronoi network mode uses a true 3x3 window.

critic.notes: Good-looking at the default on every seed I tried, but the troughs read as smooth canals and the tributary tiers do not read as a branching system; the wide view keeps closed loops. The gain over a stock F2-F1 carve is gradient-normalised width, which is the iso-distance kernel another family already provides. Cost is 3 tiers of 1 + dim valley evals plus the source. Ship the fjord blocks tree as a preset and, if iso-distance ships, a saved graph of it.

tournament.notes: Re-measured: c0ratio 2.17, max slope 45.6 (steep walls, continuous by the prototyper's step test), range -0.944..1.095, far coords fine, scalar 1179 ns (23.8x perlin2, 10.8x worley2). The default holds on new seeds: a big bending fjord with a flat floor at 2024, a trough along the edge with lakes at 99, several long straight U troughs crossing the massif at window 16. But the troughs read as smooth canals cut through rough mountains, tributaries do not read as branching, and closed loops remain. The prototyper's own stock F2-F1 carve graph gives fjord blocks about as convincing, and the only gain is gradient-normalised width, which the iso-distance kernel of another family already provides. Ship the fjord blocks tree as a preset.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 18 ns in 2D with a 6 octave source; in 3D about 27 ns plus source; in 4D about 65 ns plus source (3 tiers of 1 + dim Perlin evals).

artist-terrain.note: Fjord relief is striking, troughs read as smooth canals through rough mountains; 24x Perlin scalar; stock fjord-blocks graph rivals it.

artist-material.note: U valleys with lakes look terrific in relief. A stock graph gets a similar fjord, and it costs about 24x Perlin scalar.

voxel-engineer.note: Strong relief with U valleys, reads as canals, and a stock fjord graph competes.

maintainer.note: Fjord floor view is striking but the critic shows a warped F2-F1 / PowFloat / Min two-tier stock graph gets the fjord blocks; 18-65 ns est, c0 2.8.

graphics-researcher.note: Fjord floor reads as glaciated country, but 24x Perlin, c0 2.2, and a stock fjord-blocks graph gets the massif-with-troughs character.

creative.note: One of the most believable landscapes in the whole set, with clear U valleys.

master.one_liner: Carves U-shaped troughs of constant world width along a source's zero contours, with raised floors per tier so hanging valleys and truncated spurs emerge from a simple Min.
master.look: Yosemite and fjord-like valleys: flat floors, near-vertical walls, cut spurs, side valleys that end in mid-wall. Setting Floor below sea level makes winding fjord systems with islands.
master.algorithm: For tier t in 0..T-1: n=ValleySource(p*scale_t, seed+t), grad by forward differences, d=|n|/max(|grad|,eps). Trough surface U_t=Floor(p)+Hang*t+Dt*min((d/W_t)^q,1) with q about 2-4 and W_t=W*r^t. Ice gate: e=smoothstep(ELA-b,ELA+b,h(p)), so only high ground is glaciated: h'=lerp(h, min(h,U_t), e_t), applied sequentially. Since Min simply cuts through spurs, spurs truncate into straight faces. A smaller tier with a higher floor ends abruptly on a parent's wall as a hanging valley, and waterfalls are implied there.
master.why_new: Ridged and Abs-based valleys are V-shaped, widening with low slope. Constant-width U and tiered floors require gradient normalisation unavailable to graphs. Hanging valleys normally suggest simulation, but here they arise from a Min of independent surfaces.
master.simd_plan: T x (dim+1) Valley evals + h + hybrids; 3 tiers in 2D with single Perlin valleys is 9 Perlin evals plus source, about 10-15 ns plus h. GenT works for 2D, 3D and 4D and preserves tiling when sources tile.
master.continuity: C0: min and lerp of continuous fields; d uses the eps floor.
master.params: Source, Valley Source, Tiers (int), Width and Width Ratio r, Hang (float), Depth, Sharpness q, Floor (hybrid), ELA, ELA Blend, Tier Scale.
master.risks: Not tested. Zero contours of noise form closed loops rather than trees, so the pattern might look like lakes or moats unless warped or stretched. Near-zero gradient on contour is rare but gives wide troughs. Overlaps some ContourScarp machinery; could share a helper.
master.cost_note: T x (dim+1) Valley evals + h + hybrids; 3 tiers in 2D with single Perlin valleys is 9 Perlin evals plus source, about 10-15 ns plus h.
